messages:
alice_sales: We're blocked on Acme POC — Okta provisioning shows 403 when posting to SCIM and SAML responses are rejected. They say Dedicated pool + VPC ready but users not created. Anyone available to triage?

tom_se: Can you grab the Okta provisioning log line and the SAML Response (SAML tracer)? Common culprits: wrong SCIM base URL (hosted vs tenant), or Audience/ACS mismatch.

alice_sales: Pasted the Okta error: `POST https://api.redwood.example.com/scim/v2/Users 403` and SAML: `Audience mismatch (expected https://redwood.example.com/tenants/T-abc/acs)` — looks like they used hosted URL.

rachel_solutions: Yep — Dedicated tenants require tenant-scoped endpoints. Ask them to point Okta to `https://api.redwood.example.com/tenants/<tenant_id>/scim/v2/`. Also confirm SCIM token belongs to that tenant (token scope is tenant-bound).

tom_se: Quick manual test they can run:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCIM_TOKEN" -H "Accept: application/scim+json" \
  "https://api.redwood.example.com/tenants/T-abc/scim/v2/Users"
```
Should return 200. If 403, check token and tenant id.

alice_sales: They ran the curl and got 403. They pasted token masked.

rachel_solutions: Next checks: 1) Did we rotate SAML cert recently? If so they need new metadata. 2) VPC allowlist — our agent IPs must be allowed from their side or the reverse, depending on routing. A network block can cause weird 403-ish behavior if a proxy returns that.

tom_se: I'll rotate the SAML cert if it's near expiry and generate new metadata. Also will validate the tenant id mapping in Console -> Tenant settings.

alice_sales: Temporary workaround requested by customer: can we manually create the 3 demo users in the Dedicated env so they can demo features tomorrow?

rachel_solutions: We can create them manually. Also opening POC ticket and assigning to tom_se.

integration-bot: Ticket POC-2024 created and assigned to tom_se; logs attached.

alice_sales: Thanks — I'll set up a short troubleshooting call and share the Okta admin screen during the call.
